\section[a declaração]{a declaração — the declaration, the public statement}

\label{lesson:PT-C282-declaracao}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the written report, then the Portuguese for to announce in the news.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a declaração}
\textbf{a declaração} — \textquotedblleft{}the declaration, the public statement\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O presidente fez uma declaração aos jornalistas.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The president made a statement to the journalists.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Fazer uma declaração} — to make a statement. Also a form you fill in.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{declaração} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{dēclārātiō} \textquotedblleft{}a making clear\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from \emph{dēclārāre}, built on \emph{clārus} \textquotedblleft{}clear\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{a declaração}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{a declaração}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{a declaração}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for the written report, then the Portuguese for to announce in the news, then say \emph{a declaração} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does a declaração mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The declaration, the public statement\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[o comentário]{o comentário — the comment, the remark}

\label{lesson:PT-C282-comentario}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to announce in the news, then the Portuguese for the declaration.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o comentário}
\textbf{o comentário} — \textquotedblleft{}the comment, the remark\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O presidente não fez nenhum comentário.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The president made no comment.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Sem comentários} — no comment.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{comentário} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{commentārium} \textquotedblleft{}notes, a commentary\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), related to \emph{comminīscī} \textquotedblleft{}to devise\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for to announce in the news, then the Portuguese for the declaration, then say \emph{o comentário} again

\section[confirmar]{confirmar — to confirm}

\label{lesson:PT-C282-confirmar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the declaration, then the Portuguese for the comment.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: confirmar}
\textbf{confirmar} — \textquotedblleft{}to confirm\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
A escola confirmou a data da festa.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The school confirmed the date of the party.}
\end{quote}

Also to confirm a booking: \emph{confirmar a reserva}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{confirmar} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{cōnfirmāre} \textquotedblleft{}to strengthen, to make sure\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{firmus} \textquotedblleft{}firm\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for the declaration, then the Portuguese for the comment, then say \emph{confirmar} again
\end{itemize}

\section[o comunicado]{o comunicado — the press release, the official notice}

\label{lesson:PT-C282-comunicado}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the comment, then the Portuguese for to confirm.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o comunicado}
\textbf{o comunicado} — \textquotedblleft{}the press release, the official notice\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O clube divulgou um comunicado no site.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The club put out a press release on its website.}
\end{quote}

A short official text sent to the media.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{comunicado} is the past participle of \emph{comunicar} used as a noun; the verb comes from Latin \emph{commūnicāre} \textquotedblleft{}to share\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{commūnis} \textquotedblleft{}common\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[o comentador]{o comentador — the commentator, the pundit}

\label{lesson:PT-C282-comentador}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to confirm, then the Portuguese for the press release.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o comentador}
\textbf{o comentador} — \textquotedblleft{}the commentator, the pundit\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Na televisão, um comentador explicou os resultados.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{On television a pundit explained the results.}
\end{quote}

Portugal’s TV is full of \emph{comentadores} of politics and football. A woman is \emph{a comentadora}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{comentador} is built on \emph{comentar}, a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{commentārī} \textquotedblleft{}to think over, to study\textquotedblright{}; Latin itself had \emph{commentātor} \textquotedblleft{}a deviser, an interpreter\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for to confirm, then the Portuguese for the press release, then say \emph{o comentador} again
